title: Transgenic Tomato Line Generation via Agrobacterium tumefaciens Transformation
author: Mountourakis, Fragkostefanakis, et al.
materials:
Timing: 1 h
1.Prepare the following stock solutions (1,000x concentrated):a.Trans-zeatin: 2 mg/mL in water (filter sterilize, store at −20°C).b.Acetosyringone: 100 mM in dimethyl sulfoxide - DMSO (store at −20°C).c.Timentin™: 500 mg/mL in water (filter-sterilize, store at −20°C).d.Commonly used selection antibiotics: Rifampicin in DMSO 25 mg/mL (light sensitive, store at −20°C), Gentamycin 50 mg/mL in water (filter-sterilize, store at −20°C) Kanamycin: 50 mg/mL in water (filter-sterilize, store at −20°C), Hygromycin B: 5 mg/mL (light sensitive, filter-sterilize, store at −20°C).
Note: Prepare all stock solutions under sterile conditions. Filter-sterilize heat-labile components using 0.2 μm PES filters. Protect light sensitive components using aluminum foil or black tubes.

steps.title: Prepare 1000× Stock Solutions
steps.instruction: Under sterile conditions, make the following 1,000× stocks and store as indicated: trans‑zeatin 2 mg/mL in water (filter‑sterilize, −20 °C); acetosyringone 100 mM in DMSO (−20 °C); Timentin™ 500 mg/mL in water (filter‑sterilize, −20 °C); Rifampicin 25 mg/mL in DMSO (light‑sensitive, −20 °C); Gentamycin 50 mg/mL in water (filter‑sterilize, −20 °C); Kanamycin 50 mg/mL in water (filter‑sterilize, −20 °C); Hygromycin B 5 mg/mL in water (light‑sensitive, filter‑sterilize, −20 °C). Use 0.2 µm PES filters for heat‑labile components and protect light‑sensitive stocks with aluminum foil or black tubes.

steps.title: Make Germination Medium (MS/2)
steps.instruction: Prepare liquid MS/2 medium: weigh 2.15 g MS salts into a 1 L beaker, add 900 mL Milli‑Q water, stir, adjust pH to 5.8 with 1 M KOH, bring volume to 1 L, aliquot 100 mL into ten 200 mL bottles, autoclave (121 °C, 20 min), cool below 50 °C before use. For solid MS/2 add 0.6 g plant agar per 100 mL before autoclaving; store at 23 ± 2 °C for weeks. No sucrose is added.

steps.title: Prepare Yeast Extract Peptone Medium
steps.instruction: Prepare liquid YEP: weigh 10 g yeast extract into a 1 L bottle, add 900 mL Milli‑Q water, stir, add 10 g peptone, add 5 g NaCl, adjust pH to 7 with 1 M KOH, bring to 1 L, dispense 100 mL into ten 200 mL bottles, autoclave (121 °C, 20 min), cool below 50 °C, then add antibiotics as required (e.g., Rifampicin 25 µg/mL, Gentamycin 50 µg/mL, Kanamycin 50 µg/mL). For solid YEP add 1.5 g agar per 100 mL before autoclaving; store at 23 ± 2 °C for weeks.

steps.title: Prepare Preculture Co‑cultivation Medium (2ZA)
steps.instruction: Make liquid 2ZA: add 3 g sucrose per 100 mL of liquid MS/2, stir, adjust pH to 5.5 with 1 M KOH, autoclave (121 °C, 20 min), cool below 50 °C, add 100 µL per 100 mL trans‑zeatin stock (final 2 µg/mL) and 100 µL per 100 mL acetosyringone stock (final 100 µM). For solid 2ZA add 0.6 g plant agar per 100 mL before autoclaving; store plates at 2–8 °C for 1–2 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare Regeneration Media (2Z…)
steps.instruction: Prepare liquid regeneration base as for 2ZA (3 g sucrose per 100 mL, pH 5.5, autoclave, cool). Add 100 µL per 100 mL trans‑zeatin stock (2 µg/mL). Then add antibiotics according to the desired formulation: • 2Z500T – 100 µL per 100 mL Timentin stock (final 500 µg/mL). • 2Z500TK – 100 µL per 100 mL Timentin (500 µg/mL) plus 100 µL per 100 mL Kanamycin stock (50 µg/mL). • 2Z250TK – 50 µL per 100 mL Timentin (250 µg/mL) plus 100 µL per 100 mL Kanamycin stock (50 µg/mL). For solid versions add 0.6 g plant agar per 100 mL before autoclaving; prepare fresh and store at 2–8 °C for 1–2 weeks.

steps.title: Prepare Rooting Medium (250TMS1/2)
steps.instruction: Make liquid rooting medium: add 1 g sucrose per 100 mL of liquid MS/2, stir, autoclave, cool below 50 °C, add 50 µL per 100 mL Timentin stock (final 250 µg/mL). For solid medium add 0.6 g plant agar per 100 mL before autoclaving; prepare fresh and store at 2–8 °C for 1–2 weeks.

steps.title: Cultivate Agrobacterium for Transformation
steps.instruction: Start from a fresh plate of Agrobacterium tumefaciens carrying the binary plasmid (or from a –80 °C glycerol stock, 20 % v/v). In a sterile 200 mL Erlenmeyer flask add 50 mL liquid YEP medium and the appropriate antibiotics (Rifampicin, Gentamycin, Kanamycin as needed). Inoculate with the Agrobacterium and incubate for 2 days at 28 °C with shaking at 200 rpm.

steps.title: Harvest and Adjust Bacterial Suspension
steps.instruction: Transfer the 2‑day culture to a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube and centrifuge at 1,000 g for 20 min at 23 ± 2 °C. Discard the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL freshly prepared 2ZA medium. Measure OD₆₀₀ and dilute with the same 2ZA medium to obtain an OD₆₀₀ of 0.2–0.4 (use the same buffer as blank). Approximately 25 mL of this suspension is needed per full Petri plate of tomato cotyledon/hypocotyl pieces; 1–2 Falcon tubes are sufficient for the step.

steps.title: Acclimate Bacteria Before Infection
steps.instruction: Incubate the adjusted bacterial suspension for 1–2 h in the dark at 23 ± 2 °C on a shaker. Wrap the conical tubes in aluminum foil or use black tubes, keep the volume ≤ 25 mL per 50‑mL tube, loosen the caps slightly and secure with tape to allow gas exchange.

steps.title: Inoculate Tomato Explants
steps.instruction: Place excised tomato cotyledon and hypocotyl pieces in an empty sterile Petri dish, add enough liquid bacterial culture to cover them, wrap tightly with aluminum foil and place on a shaker at 23 ± 2 °C with mild rocking (~100 rpm, 3 mm orbital radius) for ~30 min. Using a sterile gauge, blot excess liquid from the explants and immediately transfer them to fresh 2ZA medium.

steps.title: Co‑cultivate Explants
steps.instruction: Wrap the Petri dishes containing the inoculated explants with aluminum foil and incubate in the dark for 2 days at 20–22 °C. Do not exceed 25 °C, as higher temperatures markedly reduce Agrobacterium virulence.

description: Tissue culture remains a fundamental and indispensable technique in contemporary plant biotechnology due to its proven capacity to provide reproducible regeneration of genetically uniform and stable transgenic plants. Despite advances in genome editing methods like virus-induced techniques that can reduce reliance on tissue culture, it is still the gold standard for crops like tomato. The protocol below describes the specific steps for Agrobacterium tumefaciens-mediated stable transformation of tomato, optimized for the cultivar MicroTom and Kanamycin selection marker. However, we have efficiently applied the same protocol for Hygromycin B selection marker and other tomato cultivars like Moneymaker, obtaining similar results in terms of time efficiency and successful generation of transgenic lines.
